is an association football sports video game developed by Tamsoft and published by Bandai Namco Entertainment for Microsoft Windows , Nintendo Switch and PlayStation 4 in August 2020. It is based on the 2018 anime series Captain Tsubasa . Gameplay [ edit ] Captain Tsubasa: Rise of New Champions includes offline and online multiplayer modes, and a single-player story mode split into two sub-modes: Episode Tsubasa, [ 1 ] allowing players to experience the original storyline, and Episode New Hero, [ 2 ] allowing players to create their character and level up in a fashion similar to the FIFA series ' Player Career mode or Pro Evolution Soccer ' s Become A Legend mode. In New Hero, players can choose to represent Nankatsu Middle School, Furano Middle School, Toho Academy, Musashi Middle School, Otomo Middle School, or Hanawa Middle School before playing in the Junior Youth World Challenge, an international U-16 tournament. Plot [ edit ] [</span>icon<span typeof=\"mw:Entity\" id=\"mwKg\">]</span>","txt":"[icon]"}]]}'> This section needs expansion . You can help by adding missing information . ( April 2025 ) The game follows two distinct plotlines: firstly, "Episode Tsubasa" retraces Tsubasa Oozora 's goal to achieve a three-peat at the 16th National School Tournament, while its sequel, "Episode New Hero", follows the player's custom made avatar joining one of different middle school then forming the All-Japan national soccer team to win the Junior Youth World Challenge, an international U-16 tournament. Episode Tsubasa [ edit ] The story begins with Tsubasa Oozora training with his team, Nankatsu MS. Among the players present are hotheaded defender Ryo Ishizaki, cowardly determined goalkeeper Yuzo Morisaki and grand-framed defender Shingo Takasugi, alongside three players forming the "Shutetsu Trio", consisting of midfielder and heading expert Mamoru Izawa, forward and main scorer Teppei Kisugi and forward and sideline specialist Hajime Taki. As the team trains, they are interrupted and defeated by the Otomo Quartet, the four main players of rival middle school Otomo: the quartet consists of midfielder and captain Hanji Urabe, defenders Masao Nakayama and Koji Nishio and midfielder Takeshi Kishida. As they depart, Nankatsu soon encounters Kojiro Hyuga, a forward and captain for Toho Academy known for his relentlessly aggressive play and long-lasting childhood rivalry against Tsubasa: he swears to him that he will defeat Nankatsu for good after having lost the two previous iterations of the 16 Middle School National Tournament, of which Nankatsu won both times against Toho in the finals. After defeating Otomo in the Shizuoka Prefecture Finals, Nankatsu advances to the 16th Middle School National Tournament, where Toho was playing against Musashi, led by midfielder Jun Misugi, also known as the "Young Noble" for his well-executed and graceful plays. Shortly before the match ends, Misugi, through a series of passes from his teammates, attempts to score a goal against Toho, since Musashi was behind in points: however, Ken Wakashimazu, Toho's goalkeeper known for using his karate techninques in a soccer match, barely catches the shot one-handedly, thus ending the match with Toho winning 3-2. However, due to Misugi's heart failure, Hyuga falters slightly as a tiger whihout fangs, which gets criticized by his mentor Kozo Kira, who forces him to train in Okinawa, where Hyuga develops his "Tiger Shot" skill by breaking through the waves with the ball. However, the Toho coach Makoto Kitazume, known for his strict teaching and a self-made set of convictions he abides to. Learns about Hyuga's trip and gets angry. As Hyuga arrives for 16th Middle School National Tournament after devolping his Tiger Shot, Kitazume berates and punishes him by benching him for the duration of the tournament. Development [ edit ] Rise of New Champions was developed by Tamsoft , [ 3 ] based on the 2018 anime series Captain Tsubasa , [ 4 ] and produced by Tsuzuki Katsuaki, who described the game design as similar to arcade soccer games. [ 5 ] The game was released [ 6 ] by Bandai Namco Entertainment in 2020 in Japan for Nintendo Switch and PlayStation 4 on August 27, [ 7 ] [ 8 ] and internationally for Microsoft Windows , Nintendo Switch and PlayStation 4 the very next day on August 28. [ 3 ] Marketing [ edit ] In April 2021, Bandai Namco Europe and the Ligue de Football Professionnel began a partnership through which 17 of the 20 2020-21 Ligue 1 clubs (not including Paris Saint-Germain FC , Olympique Lyonnais and Olympique de Marseille ) had their kits unlockable through a two-week event in April and May the same year. ***Captain Tsubasa: Rise of New Champions***[\[a\]](#cite_note-1) is an [association football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") [sports video game](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sports_video_game "Sports video game") developed by [Tamsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamsoft "Tamsoft") and published by [Bandai Namco Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandai_Namco_Entertainment "Bandai Namco Entertainment") for [Microsoft Windows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Windows "Microsoft Windows"), [Nintendo Switch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Switch "Nintendo Switch") and [PlayStation 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_4 "PlayStation 4") in August 2020\. It is based on the 2018 [anime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anime "Anime") series *[Captain Tsubasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_Tsubasa "Captain Tsubasa")*.

## Gameplay

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Captain_Tsubasa:_Rise_of_New_Champions&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Gameplay")\]

*Captain Tsubasa: Rise of New Champions* includes offline and online multiplayer modes, and a single-player story mode split into two sub-modes: Episode Tsubasa,[\[1\]](#cite_note-2) allowing players to experience the original storyline, and Episode New Hero,[\[2\]](#cite_note-3) allowing players to create their character and level up in a fashion similar to the [*FIFA* series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_\(video_game_series\) "FIFA (video game series)")' Player Career mode or *[Pro Evolution Soccer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro_Evolution_Soccer "Pro Evolution Soccer")*'s Become A Legend mode. In New Hero, players can choose to represent Nankatsu Middle School, Furano Middle School, Toho Academy, Musashi Middle School, Otomo Middle School, or Hanawa Middle School before playing in the Junior Youth World Challenge, an international U-16 tournament.

The game follows two distinct plotlines: firstly, "Episode Tsubasa" retraces [Tsubasa Oozora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tsubasa_Oozora "Tsubasa Oozora")'s goal to achieve a three-peat at the 16th National School Tournament, while its sequel, "Episode New Hero", follows the player's custom made avatar joining one of different middle school then forming the All-Japan national soccer team to win the Junior Youth World Challenge, an international U-16 tournament.

### Episode Tsubasa

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Captain_Tsubasa:_Rise_of_New_Champions&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Episode Tsubasa")\]

The story begins with Tsubasa Oozora training with his team, Nankatsu MS. Among the players present are hotheaded defender Ryo Ishizaki, cowardly determined goalkeeper Yuzo Morisaki and grand-framed defender Shingo Takasugi, alongside three players forming the "Shutetsu Trio", consisting of midfielder and heading expert Mamoru Izawa, forward and main scorer Teppei Kisugi and forward and sideline specialist Hajime Taki. As the team trains, they are interrupted and defeated by the Otomo Quartet, the four main players of rival middle school Otomo: the quartet consists of midfielder and captain Hanji Urabe, defenders Masao Nakayama and Koji Nishio and midfielder Takeshi Kishida. As they depart, Nankatsu soon encounters Kojiro Hyuga, a forward and captain for Toho Academy known for his relentlessly aggressive play and long-lasting childhood rivalry against Tsubasa: he swears to him that he will defeat Nankatsu for good after having lost the two previous iterations of the 16 Middle School National Tournament, of which Nankatsu won both times against Toho in the finals.

After defeating Otomo in the Shizuoka Prefecture Finals, Nankatsu advances to the 16th Middle School National Tournament, where Toho was playing against Musashi, led by midfielder Jun Misugi, also known as the "Young Noble" for his well-executed and graceful plays. Shortly before the match ends, Misugi, through a series of passes from his teammates, attempts to score a goal against Toho, since Musashi was behind in points: however, Ken Wakashimazu, Toho's goalkeeper known for using his karate techninques in a soccer match, barely catches the shot one-handedly, thus ending the match with Toho winning 3-2.

However, due to Misugi's heart failure, Hyuga falters slightly as a tiger whihout fangs, which gets criticized by his mentor Kozo Kira, who forces him to train in Okinawa, where Hyuga develops his "Tiger Shot" skill by breaking through the waves with the ball. However, the Toho coach Makoto Kitazume, known for his strict teaching and a self-made set of convictions he abides to. Learns about Hyuga's trip and gets angry. As Hyuga arrives for 16th Middle School National Tournament after devolping his Tiger Shot, Kitazume berates and punishes him by benching him for the duration of the tournament.

## Development

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Captain_Tsubasa:_Rise_of_New_Champions&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Development")\]

*Rise of New Champions* was developed by [Tamsoft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamsoft "Tamsoft"),[\[3\]](#cite_note-gem_500k-4) based on the 2018 [anime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anime "Anime") series *[Captain Tsubasa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Captain_Tsubasa "Captain Tsubasa")*,[\[4\]](#cite_note-5) and produced by Tsuzuki Katsuaki, who described the game design as similar to arcade soccer games.[\[5\]](#cite_note-6)

The game was released[\[6\]](#cite_note-7) by [Bandai Namco Entertainment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandai_Namco_Entertainment "Bandai Namco Entertainment") in 2020 in Japan for [Nintendo Switch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nintendo_Switch "Nintendo Switch") and [PlayStation 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_4 "PlayStation 4") on August 27,[\[7\]](#cite_note-8)[\[8\]](#cite_note-9) and internationally for [Microsoft Windows](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microsoft_Windows "Microsoft Windows"), Nintendo Switch and PlayStation 4 the very next day on August 28\.[\[3\]](#cite_note-gem_500k-4)

## Marketing

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Captain_Tsubasa:_Rise_of_New_Champions&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Marketing")\]

In April 2021, Bandai Namco Europe and the [Ligue de Football Professionnel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ligue_de_Football_Professionnel "Ligue de Football Professionnel") began a partnership through which 17 of the 20 2020-21 [Ligue 1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ligue_1 "Ligue 1") clubs (not including [Paris Saint-Germain FC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paris_Saint-Germain_FC "Paris Saint-Germain FC"), [Olympique Lyonnais](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympique_Lyonnais "Olympique Lyonnais") and [Olympique de Marseille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympique_de_Marseille "Olympique de Marseille")) had their kits unlockable through a two-week event in April and May the same year.[\[9\]](#cite_note-10)

The Microsoft Windows version of the game received generally positive reviews,[\[10\]](#cite_note-mc_pc-11) while the console versions were met by "mixed or average reviews", according to the [review aggregator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Review_aggregator "Review aggregator") [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic").[\[11\]](#cite_note-mc_ns-12)[\[12\]](#cite_note-mc_ps4-13) Fellow review aggregator [OpenCritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenCritic "OpenCritic") assessed that the game received fair approval, being recommended by 59% of critics.[\[13\]](#cite_note-opencritic-14)

The Nintendo Switch version of '*Rise of New Champions* was the sixth highest-selling retail game during its first week of sale in Japan, with 16,678 copies being sold. During the same week, the [PlayStation 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PlayStation_4 "PlayStation 4") version sold 13,828 copies in Japan, making it the eighth bestselling retail game of the week in the country.[\[19\]](#cite_note-21) By September 2020, over 500 000 physical and digital copies had been sold worldwide.[\[3\]](#cite_note-gem_500k-4)

## About This Game

Prince of Persia creator Jordan Mechner was a college student when he created one of the biggest-selling games of 1984: Karateka. Now, in a new interactive documentary from Digital Eclipse, the story of how a teenager with an Apple II created one of the most groundbreaking, influential games of all time.  
  
**THE ORIGIN STORY OF A LEGENDARY GAME CREATOR**  
  
Discover how Karateka was made through an exhaustive archive of design documents, playable prototypes, and all-new video features. Like walking through a museum, you can explore the interactive timelines at your own pace.  
  
**PLAY THE ACCLAIMED ORIGINALS**  
  
Enjoy pixel-perfect versions of the original Karateka games and a variety of never-before-seen early prototypes, with rich quality-of-life features like save anywhere, rewind, chapter select, and director's commentary.  
  
**TWO REMASTERED GAMES**  
  
Karateka Remastered is an all-new version of the original game featuring cutting-room-floor content, commentary, achievements, and more. Deathbounce: Rebounded is a fast and frantic twin-stick shooter based on Jordan's unpublished prototype.  
  
**A GROUNDBREAKING MASTERPIECE**  
  
Discover how Karateka became one of the first games to include cinematic scenes, a moving original soundtrack, rotoscoped animation, and a Hollywood-style love story, influencing the decades of games that followed.  
  
**THE GOLD MASTER SERIES**  
  
New from Digital Eclipse (Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Cowabunga Collection, Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration), the Gold Master Series presents iconic games in an innovative "interactive documentary" format, putting the shared history of games and their creators into one comprehensive package.

## Process lifecycle

- Run long-lived servers and watchers in a persistent session such as tmux.
- Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
- After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

## Linux browser and WebGPU capture

- Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
- Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
- Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
- Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
- Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
- Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
- Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.
- Inspect `$HOME/.local/share/omgithub-playwright/linux.json` for launch settings.
- Use `playwright-cli --help` for commands and named sessions. Pass configuration only to `open`.

## Mobile browser games

- Support Android and iOS phones and tablets with responsive layouts and usable touch controls.
- Keep gameplay and controls visible within safe areas and avoid browser gesture conflicts.
- Add tilt controls only when appropriate; offer touch alternatives and request iOS motion permission from a user gesture when needed.

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw, ImageFont
import os

OUT='/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/cards'
os.makedirs(OUT, exist_ok=True)

W,H=540,726
font_bold='/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/LiberationSans-Bold.ttf'
font_reg='/usr/share/fonts/truetype/liberation/LiberationSans-Regular.ttf'

def card(name, pos, ovr, stats, playstyle, ability, potential, title, filename):
    img=Image.new('RGB',(W,H),(18,22,30))
    d=ImageDraw.Draw(img)
    # background gradient-ish
    for y in range(H):
        t=y/H
        r=int(18+ (40-18)*t)
        g=int(22+ (30-22)*t)
        b=int(30+ (55-30)*t)
        d.line([(0,y),(W,y)],fill=(r,g,b))
    # border
    d.rectangle([8,8,W-9,H-9],outline=(200,170,60),width=4)
    # OVR
    f_ovr=ImageFont.truetype(font_bold,120)
    d.text((40,30),str(ovr),font=f_ovr,fill=(255,215,0))
    # position
    f_pos=ImageFont.truetype(font_bold,34)
    d.text((40,160),pos,font=f_pos,fill=(220,220,220))
    # name
    f_name=ImageFont.truetype(font_bold,42)
    d.text((40,230),name,font=f_name,fill=(255,255,255))
    # stats
    labels=['SHO','PAC','DEF','PAS','PHY','DRI']
    vals=[stats[l] for l in labels]
    f_lab=ImageFont.truetype(font_bold,26)
    f_val=ImageFont.truetype(font_bold,40)
    y0=320
    for i,(lab,val) in enumerate(zip(labels,vals)):
        x=40 + (i%3)*170
        y=y0 + (i//3)*110
        d.text((x,y),lab,font=f_lab,fill=(180,180,180))
        d.text((x,y+35),str(val),font=f_val,fill=(255,255,255))
    # playstyle etc
    f_small=ImageFont.truetype(font_reg,24)
    y=560
    d.text((40,y),f'Playstyle: {playstyle}',font=f_small,fill=(200,200,200)); y+=35
    d.text((40,y),f'Ability: {ability}',font=f_small,fill=(200,200,200)); y+=35
    d.text((40,y),f'Potential: {potential}',font=f_small,fill=(200,200,200)); y+=35
    d.text((40,y),f'Title: {title}',font=f_small,fill=(200,200,200)); y+=35
    img.save(os.path.join(OUT,filename))
    print('saved',filename)
